answers.bix-10-q1: In the multivariable ordinal logistic regression including patients_seen_cat and expect_interact_cat, the odds ratio for higher COVID-19 severity for BCG vs placebo is 1.29.
answers.bix-10-q2: In the adjusted ordinal logistic regression (controlling for patients_seen_cat and TRTGRP_cat), the odds ratio for higher COVID-19 severity for healthcare workers who expect to interact with patients (Yes vs No) is 1.03.
answers.bix-10-q3: None of the patient volume groups (1–50, 51–100, >100 patients) show a statistically significant (p<0.05) difference in COVID-19 severity between BCG and placebo by chi-square test.
answers.bix-10-q4: The chi-square p-value for the association between BCG vaccination and COVID-19 severity among healthcare workers who expect to interact with patients is 0.0424 (approximately).
answers.bix-10-q5: For healthcare workers seeing >100 patients, the chi-square p-value for the association between vaccination status and disease severity is 0.4142.
answers.bix-10-q6: For healthcare workers seeing 1–50 patients, the chi-square p-value for the association between vaccination status and disease severity is 0.0735.
answers.bix-10-q7: Because the adjusted odds ratio for higher COVID-19 severity for workers who expect to interact with patients (Yes vs No) is 1.03, there is effectively 0% reduction (a slight, non-significant 3% increase) in odds rather than a reduction.
